title: Malicious Packages Steal Cloud Credentials From CI/CD Pipelines and Developer Workstations at Install Time
content_md: Malicious software packages can steal cloud credentials during installation, exposing developer workstations and continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) pipelines before an application runs. These attacks turn routine dependency updates into potential entry points for cloud account compromise. The threat centers on installation scripts that execute with the permissions of the developer or build runner. A successful build does not prove the environment is safe. Malicious code may already have collected secrets and sent them to infrastructure controlled by attackers. Developer environments often contain AWS access keys, GitHub tokens, Azure credentials, Google Cloud service account keys, Kubernetes configuration files, and npm publishing tokens. When these secrets carry broad permissions, a compromised dependency can expose resources far beyond the affected software project. Malicious Packages Steal Credentials The supplied research describes campaigns targeting trusted packages and development tools across npm, RubyGems, Go, PyPI, and container registries. Their shared approach is to execute malicious code, harvest available credentials, and use those credentials to expand access. The Shai-Hulud campaign illustrates this pattern. According to the supplied material, infected npm packages searched developer and build environments for secrets.
